quotes.quote: Kimi K3 is evaluated with both the Kimi Code and Claude Code harnesses; GLM-5.2, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Fable 5 with the Claude Code harness; GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol with the Codex harness.
All Kimi K3 results reported below are obtained with the reasoning effort set to 'max', setting temperature = 1.0 and top-p = 1.0.
We also note that on this in-house benchmark, 10% of the tasks entered GPT-5.6 Sol's cyber guard.

Kimi Code Bench 2.0 (in-house). Kimi K3 is evaluated with the Kimi Code harness (it attains 73.7 with the Claude Code harness); GLM-5.2, Claude Opus 4.8, and Claude Fable 5 with the Claude Code harness; GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol with the Codex harness.
Claude Fable 5 hit 13 fallbacks and 1 refusal out of 80 tasks; 10 refusals out of 80 tasks entered GPT-5.6 Sol's cyber guard; GPT-5.5 had 3 refusals out of 80 tasks.

Kimi Code Bench 2.0 and Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon. These are internal benchmarks. K3.1 Pro is evaluated with Claude Code; all other models use their maximum-effort setting. Proprietary-model testing may involve fallback behavior.

And on Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon, our internal benchmark that tests coding agents' multi-step execution, tool use, and end-to-end problem solving across diverse engineering domains, K3.1 Pro scores 61.2%, above K3's 55.95%.
Internal Coding Bench: Kimi Code Bench 2.0 and Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon. Kimi K3.1 Pro is evaluated with Claude-Code harnesses; All other models are evaluated at their max-effort setting.

Beyond the public benchmark suite, we maintain a collection of in-house benchmarks that target capability areas public evaluations do not adequately cover, giving a more comprehensive measure of model and agent capabilities.
Kimi Code Bench 2.0 (KCB 2.0): evaluates code agents on realistic, end-to-end software engineering tasks across a broad range of programming languages and production-oriented technology stacks.
These benchmarks are refreshed and expanded frequently, so that they can closely track the model's evolving failure modes and directly guide data and training iterations.
On Kimi Code Bench 2.0, Kimi K3 is 4.0 points behind Claude Fable 5 at 38% of its cost, and at high effort it already matches Claude Opus 4.8's maximum-effort score at roughly one third of the cost.
Kimi Code Bench V2 is our in-house benchmark designed to evaluate coding agents on realistic tasks.

It has diversed software engineering tasks across 10+ mainstream programming languages and a full production tech stack covering tasks from internal engineering use cases, production incidents, and real-world open-source projects
with emphasis on backend services, infrastructure, performance engineering, systems programming, security, frontend development, and ML/data engineering.

Unless stated otherwise, Kimi K2.7 Code and K2.6 were tested with thinking mode enabled via Kimi Code CLI at temperature = 1.0, top-p = 0.95, and a 262,144-token context length; GPT-5.5 ran in Codex with xhigh mode, and Opus 4.8 in Claude Code with xhigh mode.
Kimi Code Bench 2.0 — Moonshot's in-house coding-agent benchmark spanning realistic engineering tasks across 10+ languages and a full production stack, including cybersecurity/safety tasks
Neither column is a head-to-head evaluation: each score is self-reported by its own vendor under its own harness.
Kimi Code Bench 2.0 是月之暗面（Moonshot AI）的内部编程智能体评测，见于 Kimi K3 技术资料。题集未公开，成绩均为厂商自报，无法独立复现。
厂商自报指标：这是单个厂商在自家发布材料中报告的评测，其他模型没有可比成绩，因此不作为独立榜单收录，只在相关模型页展示。
